analysis_refs.heading: Viewing the boards
analysis_refs.text:
**All records are samples.** Project Gutenberg IDs, titles and the Gutenberg
rights wording are real. Every paper, author, journal, DOI (the `10.5555` test
prefix), arXiv ID and children's story is invented. Never copy board records
into fixtures as if they were real catalog data.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Navigation and routes
analysis_refs.text: | Papers | Articles, preprints, chapters (`kinds` = article, preprint, chapter, thesis, report). Query field also accepts DOI and arXiv IDs. |

analysis_refs.heading: 4. Boards
analysis_refs.text: | `PaperResults` | Paper results with type pill, title, authors, container/year, and access line naming index and host. | Pill from `kind` (+ `version` for preprints: "Preprint · v3"). Source-supplied flags ("Correction listed", "Retracted") as a second pill in `--chk`/`--err`, worded as the source's claim. Access line: "Free · Found via [index], read at [host]" when they differ; "Free · HTML, PDF at arXiv" when the index is the host. Authors truncate to three plus "+ N". |

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text:
Also investigate DOAJ, CORE/OpenAIRE/BASE, national libraries, professional
associations and ministry directories as leads. Choose an aggregator only after
checking current external-use terms, quotas, origin attribution and completeness.
Existing direct arXiv/DOAJ deferral remains in force until its stated constraint
has a supported solution; this plan does not quietly re-enable those connectors.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Canonical model
analysis_refs.text:
1. Normalize exact DOI, ISBN-10/13 equivalence, PMID/PMCID and provider IDs. Valid DOI syntax does not establish existence.
2. Reconcile descriptions of the same identified version, retaining all locations and provenance. Conflicting authoritative metadata goes to review.
3. Keep translations, editions, chapters, abridgements and recordings separate. ISBN is edition-level; ISSN container-level. Missing ISBN is valid.
4. Preserve arXiv versions and Zenodo version DOI separately from concept/unversioned identifiers. Preprint and journal article can be related without being identical. Relations require source evidence.
5. Use title/author similarity only for candidate review or visual grouping, never authoritative merging.
6. Assign durable app IDs to persisted records; alias older source-native keys rather than breaking links after reconciliation.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: FCD01: contract decisions
analysis_refs.text:
- Content keys use `fcd:v1:<source>:<record>`; Gutenberg records are positive
  integer IDs; Europe PMC records include their source (`MED`, `PMC`, `PPR`).
  A DOI is an identifier, never an app key. Versions, translations, chapters and
  recordings retain distinct source-native keys. No fuzzy-title merge.
- Reviewed StoryWeaver translations use distinct native story IDs. The pilot
  requires English/Hindi/Tamil records with original credits, publisher levels
  and per-record review evidence before enablement.
- An omitted `kinds` searches books/learning resources. Paper searches supply
  paper kinds explicitly. Mixed book/paper requests are reported unsupported;
  the API never silently omits one requested scope.
- Search and resolve both accept `country` (ISO alpha-2 or absent/unknown) and
  language context. An observation for one explicit country does not establish
  availability in another. Gutenberg's US rights statement is retained with a
  generic country-rules prompt, not turned into a global legal claim.
- A reading action requires an explicit per-location `free_full_text` claim,
  positive evidence field/source/time, a safe supplied HTTP(S) URL, and an
  observation no older than 24 hours. Stale, missing, contradictory or
  country-mismatched observations become unknown; fetch failure is not absence.
  Reuse licence and free reading remain distinct. Missing licence never becomes
  an invented Creative Commons licence.
- `not_selected` means the planner did not query this source; `disabled` means
  it is not connected. `ok` with zero results is distinct from timeout,
  unavailable, throttled and quota-exhausted. Counts describe loaded items,
  never a federated global total.
- Default results contain anonymous free full text and a separately labelled verified free-account group (owner clarification 2026-11-01). An explicit unclear group may
  contain unknown/metadata-only items with labelled source links; previews,
  borrowing, unknown-price registration and restricted access stay excluded in v1.
- Source cursors remain server-owned. Browser tokens bind query, context,
  policy/index revisions and expiry. Shared live quota reservation and page
  advancement must pass a two-instance test before a live source is enabled.
  A memory implementation is a development/test adapter only; store failure
  disables uncapped live dispatch while keeping local metadata searchable.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

verify its free allowance, accepted endpoint pricing and zero prepaid balance

No paid fallback or paid infrastructure is introduced. Normal hosting usage

- The comparison fixtures are explicitly synthetic for papers/stories; they do
  not establish source access or represent the actual reviewed children's set.

- Sources, counts, levels and available relations differ from the board samples.

  local storage, an account, analytics or a server history store.

  headers as the app API. This avoids engine-dependent buffering/routing in the

  session. Firefox was not run locally. Remote CI covers WebKit as well.

  scheduled refresh remain the previously recorded release gates. No flags,

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Begin with universities, public educational broadcasters and
institutional media producers, following their series/catalog links. In India,
[NPTEL's course catalog](https://nptel.ac.in/courses) provides instructor/course
and institutional discovery leads; investigate official educational broadcaster
and university series alongside it. For international and US material, inspect
university lecture catalogs and public-media learning collections. The
[Internet Archive developer portal](https://archive.org/developers/) documents
metadata tools for archive-hosted media; [Wikimedia Commons API guidance](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:API)
supports another metadata route, with license and exclusion markers to review.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer documented catalogs, attributed archive records
or permitted RSS/Atom imports. NPTEL's visible catalog does not establish an
external API in this review. Preserve episode/lecture ID, series/course relation,
producer, language, date, duration and canonical playback URL. Test a complete
recording, removed media, country restriction, premium-only episode and a caption
or transcript where available. Metadata search must not be described as searching
every spoken word. Hosting on an archive or public platform does not establish
lawful free access for every upload. Deep-review one feed-based producer and one
catalog-based producer before selecting a reusable media connector.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
The planner selects at most three live providers. Biomedical terms prefer
Europe PMC; general queries prefer the broad source and arXiv; DOAJ supplies
OA journal coverage. Recognized arXiv identifiers select arXiv. Sources not
chosen are explicit and can be searched independently from the source sheet.
DOIs select DOI-capable indexes; PMCIDs select Europe PMC using its PMCID field,
preserving the article's native MED identity. Bare versioned legacy arXiv IDs
also route directly to arXiv.
Language context is only supported by the broad adapter today; other paper
sources report unsupported rather than silently ignoring it.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Multi-source papers follow-up
analysis_refs.text:
DOAJ, arXiv and OpenAlex now have bounded adapters, source-native identities and
per-location access/licence handling. Fresh [policy observations](evidence/2026-11-01/source-policies.json)
verify DOAJ's 2 RPS and arXiv's 3-second/single-connection aggregate rules. The
configured OpenAlex key reported $1/day free allowance, $0.001 ordinary search
and zero prepaid funds; runtime rechecks those conditions before dispatch.
Operational limits and caveats are in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md).

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
[HEAD/header-only sampling](evidence/2026-11-01/host-head-checks.json) returned
200 from the textbook, DOAJ publisher, arXiv and Europe PMC hosts. It found a
Gutenberg legacy HTML 404; GET response headers confirmed it. The supplied direct
HTML and EPUB routes returned 200. Importer v2 removes virtual HTML links and
uses supplied direct HTML/landing URLs; a fresh 1,000-record import and runtime
audit passed. The primary location's licence and downloads now stay together;
other hosts/versions retain their own licence, and retraction flags appear on
direct detail visits. No full-text content was stored.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
Reading actions
analysis_refs.text: Show index and host separately when useful, e.g. Found via DOAJ / Read at publisher. Preserve required attribution. Broken PDF links should fall back to evidenced landing/alternate locations, never invented files. Expose freshness/country limits in details. A public-domain US scan is not a universal legal-access assertion.

analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: C03 — Published research articles
analysis_refs.text:
**Start with publisher and repository discovery, then prove individual holdings.**
[OpenDOAR](https://opendoar.ac.uk/help/about) supplies institutional repository
leads. [SciELO](https://www.scielo.org/en/) supplies country, publisher and subject
entry points, particularly useful for Latin American and regional-language
coverage. DOAJ remains a directory lead; the current direct DOAJ connector
deferral is unchanged. Separate the publisher, journal collection, repository
copy and index that found it.

analysis_refs.heading: 1. Goal and counting rules
analysis_refs.text:
Use 20 research categories: five core areas and 15 additions. Target 100 qualified
sources per category over successive research cycles. These are overlapping
category memberships, potentially 2,000 memberships, not necessarily 2,000 unique
sources or 2,000 custom integrations. Report the global unique count separately.

Also investigate DOAJ, CORE/OpenAIRE/BASE, national libraries, professional
associations and ministry directories as leads. Choose an aggregator only after

analysis_refs.heading: From a directory entry to something the app can query
analysis_refs.text:
1. **Official document/dataset catalog API.** [GovInfo documents an API search
   service](https://www.govinfo.gov/features/search-service-overview) for content
   and metadata. The current [Data.gov Catalog API](https://resources.data.gov/catalog-api/)
   searches dataset metadata and identifies publisher organizations; it explicitly
   replaces the previous CKAN API. Use the current interface and key policy,
   not an old tutorial. An indexed dataset still needs a valid resource link.
2. **Approved exports and local metadata search.** Small DCAT/CSV/JSON/XML catalogs
   can become bounded, reviewed search artifacts without a hosted database. Prefer
   metadata and canonical outbound links; do not copy whole national parcel or
   imagery stores to make a prototype searchable.
3. **Native record or feature queries.** A source can qualify for property or
   spatial lookup through real address/parcel/document-ID/area queries even when
   it lacks general keyword search. This must return record metadata and a usable
   destination; an identifier-shaped redirect to an external search page is not
   retrieval. Record this as a separate capability from topic discovery.
4. **Geo services with explicit discovery.** [OGC WFS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wfs/),
   [OGC API Features](https://www.ogc.org/standards/ogcapi-features/) and documented
   [ArcGIS layer queries](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/query-feature-service-layer/)
   are patterns to inspect for spatial/attribute filtering. Confirm the deployed
   service's capabilities, limits, IDs and terms; the platform brand is not proof.
   [WMS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wms/)/WMTS primarily deliver rendered maps
   or tiles. A searchable layer catalog can support map discovery, but does not
   establish searchable parcel attributes or downloadable source features.

This was documentation research, not an API qualification run. Current official
Data.gov, GovInfo, USGS TNM, Census, USAGov, NYC and Tamil Nadu pages were readable;
their documentation supports the proposed discovery routes, not an availability
guarantee. Data.gov's current migration notice is especially important for future
connector selection. Keys, terms, quota settings and actual result samples still
need checking before implementation.
